description: Teaches 13C tracer logic, isotopologues versus positional isotopomers, M+3 pyruvate and M+2 citrate, positional tracing, dynamic dilution, sampling and flux identifiability.
tag_paths: Label propagation from glucose into pyruvate and citrate
Isotopologues, positional labeling and alternative routes
Metabolic flux model inference and identifiability

related_resources.reason: Glucose and glutamine isotope labeling, M+2 and M+3 citrate and inference limits.
Interpretation of labeled metabolite fractions, tracer choice and ambiguity.
Tracer selection, labeled PPP carbon routing, extraction and isotope corrections.
Stable-isotope flux inference, sampling, computational modeling and uncertainty.

historical_claims.anchor: the first citrate molecules formed from labeled acetyl CoA and unlabeled oxaloacetate can have two labeled carbons.

historical_claims.anchor: Two molecules both called M plus two can carry labels in different parts of their skeletons

historical_claims.anchor: A small pyruvate pool might become fully labeled quickly even when the absolute rate is modest; a large pool might label more slowly.

authorship.scope: Original chemistry of biological networks lecture, scientific companion and source-linked metadata.

background: Introductory chemical bonding and reactions, ATP and redox carriers; specialized metabolic ideas are developed in the narration.
readiness_checks: Why does M+2 citrate not directly measure the rate of the citric acid cycle?
